title: Medical Renewal Analysis

blocks.text: We recommend staying with UnitedHealthcare Level Funded, but moving to the UHC $5,000 buy-down alternate rather than accepting the exact current-plan renewal.

The exact renewal increases to $43,088.13 per month, roughly 65% above today's cost. UHC's internal alternate reduces the monthly premium to $34,710.08 while preserving the $5,000 individual deductible, lowering the in-network out-of-pocket maximum, and avoiding a carrier change.

items.label: Approx. annual savings vs. exact renewal

blocks.text: **The important story is not the 65% headline by itself.** We tested the market broadly. Multiple underwritten carriers declined to quote, and the live outside options that did quote generally landed between roughly $39,000 and $43,000 per month at comparable benefit levels. The UHC alternate sits materially below that market range.
**What the UHC alternate gives up:** in-network coinsurance moves from 20% to 30%, and the alternate uses UHC Core rather than the broader Choice Plus network.

**What it improves:** the in-network out-of-pocket maximum drops from $8,150 to $7,000 individual, the office-visit copays remain $25 / $75, virtual care is $0, and several prescription tiers improve.

sections.heading: What the Market Is Telling Us

blocks.text: **The market response strongly validates the UHC buy-down.** Nine required carrier requests were completed. Four carriers ultimately declined to quote: Cigna Direct, Aetna AFA/Cason, Great American, and Arlo.

**Angle describes the group as favorable overall, but not uniformly low risk.** Its scorecard shows a highest composite signal around the 73rd percentile with medium variance. The primary issue is concentrated complex risk rather than broad-based poor health across the population.

items: 54% of projected annual claims cost is concentrated among members expected to exceed $10,000 in annual claims.
Clinical signals include heart failure, hypertensive heart and kidney disease, immune-related conditions, hemoglobin disorders, and chronic musculoskeletal disease.
Pharmacy signals include several branded GLP-1 therapies and other potentially high-cost medications, including Ozempic, Zepbound, Mounjaro, Wegovy, Vyepti, and Descovy.
The scorecard specifically identifies cardiorenal care management and GLP-1 pharmacy review as high-potential cost-management opportunities.

sections.heading: Claims Experience - Why the Renewal Pressure Is Real

blocks.text: **The current UHC claims report confirms that the underwriting concerns are not purely theoretical.** The plan is level funded with a $15,000 specific stop-loss deductible and a 125% aggregate corridor. The report shows meaningful large-claim activity and specific stop-loss reimbursements during the current plan year.

**In other words,** UHC has experienced real high-cost activity, while the population scorecard also shows several ongoing clinical and pharmacy risk signals. That combination helps explain both the 65% exact-plan renewal and the number of outside carriers that declined to quote.

sections.heading: Why We Would Not Take the Exact Renewal

blocks.text: **The exact current-plan renewal costs $8,378 more per month than the UHC alternate.** That is approximately $100,537 more over a full year.

items: Same $5,000 individual deductible on both plans.
The alternate actually lowers the in-network OOP maximum from $8,150 to $7,000 individual.
The alternate improves several prescription copays.
The primary sacrifices are 30% instead of 20% in-network coinsurance and moving from Choice Plus to UHC Core.

blocks.text: We do not believe those differences justify paying another $100,000+ annually.

**The one item we would verify carefully is UHC Core provider access.** The group is spread across seven states, with 53% of members in Tennessee and 82% concentrated in Tennessee, Alabama, and Florida. Before binding, we recommend checking major hospitals and any important cardiology, nephrology, hematology, rheumatology, infusion, or specialty-care providers.
**If those providers check out,** the economics strongly favor the UHC alternate.

next_steps.title: Confirm UHC Alternate
next_steps.text: Use the $34,710.08 UHC buy-down as the working renewal recommendation.

next_steps.title: Run Core Network Checks
next_steps.text: Verify key hospitals, specialists, and high-utilization providers before finalizing.

next_steps.title: Review Pharmacy
next_steps.text: Confirm important ongoing medications under the renewal formulary and look for cost-management opportunities.

next_steps.title: Move to Enrollment
next_steps.text: If network review is clean, finalize renewal paperwork and proceed into open enrollment.

bottom_line: The 65% exact-plan renewal is not the option we recommend. After a broad market review, UHC's own $5,000 buy-down is materially below the outside market, preserves the same deductible, improves the OOP maximum, and avoids the disruption of a carrier change. Given the group's concentrated high-cost risk, this is a strong renewal outcome.
